newsitem.title: FRANCE: Legrand rises on H1 results.
newsitem.headline: Legrand rises on H1 results.

text.p: Shares in French electrical retailer Legrand rose on Wednesday as the market welcomed first-half profits at the upper end of forecasts, market operators said.
The stock was up 35 francs at 820 at 1229 GMT on volume of 143,641 shares.

"The results, which were at the high end of the range, came as a nice surprise, given the current economic climate," said a fund manager. One broker said, "People were expecting very poor results, which was not the case, so the stock bounced."
The company's strong cashflow also pleased the market.
The market's current preference for cyclical stocks, on hopes of a pick up in investment in the second half of this year and growth next year, also benefited Legrand.
Legrand hit a year high of 1,005 francs per share on April 30 and has since fallen steadily, with a sharp drop between July 1 and 19 when it fell to 802 francs from 925.

The company earlier posted a 3.2 percent drop in first-half profit to 453 million francs and cashflow slightly higher at 925 million francs. It also said it did not expect significantly higher profits for 1996.
